title: Sin and the Fall
summary: How sin entered the world, what sin is, how it affects every person, and why only God can deal with it.
description: No one can understand the good news without understanding the bad news. This course studies the fall of Adam and Eve, the nature of sin, the doctrine of total depravity, original sin and its effects, the different ways Christians explain how Adam's sin affects us, and the seriousness of sin before a holy God. It ends by pointing to God's remedy in Christ.
objectives: Explain the account of the fall in Genesis 3
Define sin biblically and show its seriousness
Explain total depravity and original sin, presenting views fairly
Show that sin's only remedy is God's grace in Christ
outcomes: Describe the temptation and fall and their consequences
Define sin using key biblical words
Explain what total depravity does and does not mean
Compare the main views on how Adam's sin affects humanity
Explain sin's wages and God's gift in Christ

modules.title: The Fall
modules.intro: Genesis 3 tells how sin entered God's good world. This week we study the temptation, the fall and its immediate results.

lessons.title: The temptation
lessons.body:
God gave Adam every tree of the garden except one: "of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die" (Genesis 2:17).

The serpent questioned God's word ("Yea, hath God said?"), denied His warning ("Ye shall not surely die"), and slandered His goodness, suggesting God was holding back (Genesis 3:1-5).

Eve saw that the fruit was good for food, pleasant to the eyes, and desired to make one wise (3:6). The same pattern appears in 1 John 2:16: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life.

lessons.title: The fall and its first fruits
lessons.body:
Eve ate and gave to Adam, who ate too. At once their eyes were opened and they knew they were naked. Shame replaced innocence; they sewed fig leaves and hid from God (Genesis 3:7-8).

When God questioned them, Adam blamed Eve (and God, "the woman whom thou gavest to be with me"), and Eve blamed the serpent (3:12-13).

Sin immediately broke relationships: with God (hiding), with each other (blame), with themselves (shame), and with creation.

lessons.title: The curse and the promise
lessons.body:
God pronounced judgement: the serpent cursed; pain in childbirth and conflict in marriage for the woman; the ground cursed and toil for the man; and death: "dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return" (Genesis 3:14-19). They were driven from the garden and the tree of life (3:22-24).

Yet grace shone in judgement. God promised the woman's seed would crush the serpent's head (3:15), and He clothed them with coats of skins (3:21), a death to cover their shame.

From the beginning, God's answer to sin was a Saviour and a sacrifice.

terms.def: Adam and Eve's first sin and its fall from innocence into sin and death.

modules.title: What Is Sin?
modules.intro: Sin is more than bad behaviour. This week we see what the Bible means by sin and why it is so serious.

lessons.title: Words for sin
lessons.body:
The Bible uses many words for sin, each showing another side:

- **Missing the mark:** "all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23).
- **Transgression:** crossing a line God has drawn; "sin is the transgression of the law" (1 John 3:4).
- **Iniquity:** crookedness, twisting what is right (Isaiah 53:6).
- **Trespass:** a false step out of bounds (Ephesians 2:1).
- **Rebellion:** defiance of God's authority (1 Samuel 15:23).

At its root, sin is putting self in God's place: not loving Him with all our heart.

lessons.title: Sin in thought, word and deed
lessons.body:
Sin is not only outward acts. Jesus taught that anger is murder of the heart and lust is adultery of the heart (Matthew 5:21-28). "Out of the heart proceed evil thoughts" (Matthew 15:19).

There are sins of **commission** (doing what God forbids) and **omission** (failing to do what He commands): "to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin" (James 4:17).

Sin also includes attitudes like pride, unbelief, envy and ingratitude. "Whatsoever is not of faith is sin" (Romans 14:23).

lessons.title: Why sin is so serious
lessons.body:
Sin is serious because of whom it offends. David confessed, "Against thee, thee only, have I sinned" (Psalm 51:4). Every sin is against an infinitely holy God, who is "of purer eyes than to behold evil" (Habakkuk 1:13).

Sin brings guilt (we deserve punishment), corruption (it stains and enslaves us), and death: "the wages of sin is death" (Romans 6:23), physical death and eternal separation from God.

Sin also harms others and destroys societies. We must never call it small, nor call evil good (Isaiah 5:20).

terms.def: Any lack of conformity to, or breaking of, God's law in act, attitude or nature.

Sin includes thoughts, words, deeds, and failures to do good.

Sin is serious: it offends a holy God and brings guilt, corruption and death.

modules.title: Original Sin and Total Depravity
modules.intro: How does Adam's sin affect us, and how deeply does sin reach? This week we study original sin and depravity, including where Christians differ.

lessons.title: In Adam all die
lessons.body:
Scripture teaches that Adam's sin affected the whole human race: "by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned" (Romans 5:12). "In Adam all die" (1 Corinthians 15:22).

We are born with a sinful nature: "Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me" (Psalm 51:5). We are "by nature the children of wrath" (Ephesians 2:3).

This is called **original sin**: not that our parents sinned in conceiving us, but that we inherit a fallen condition from Adam.

lessons.title: How Adam's sin reaches us
lessons.body:
Christians agree that all inherit a sinful nature, but explain the link differently:

- **Federal (covenant) headship:** Adam acted as representative of humanity, so his guilt is counted to all, as Christ's righteousness is counted to believers (Romans 5:18-19). Common among Reformed Baptists.
- **Inherited corruption:** we inherit a corrupt nature from Adam, and become guilty when we personally sin; infants dying before accountability are saved by God's grace. Common among many Baptists, Wesleyans and Holiness churches, including Deeper Life.

Both agree that every person needs God's grace, and that God is perfectly just and good (Genesis 18:25).

lessons.title: Total depravity
lessons.body:
**Total depravity** means sin has affected every part of human nature: mind (Romans 1:21), heart (Jeremiah 17:9), will (John 8:34) and body. "There is none righteous, no, not one" (Romans 3:10).

It does **not** mean people are as evil as they could be, or that unbelievers never do anything good outwardly. God's common grace restrains sin, and people can love their children and do kind acts (Matthew 7:11).

It means that no part is untouched, and that no one can save himself or please God by his own strength (Romans 8:7-8). We need new birth.

Total depravity: sin affects every part of us, though not everyone is as evil as possible.

modules.title: Sin's Remedy
modules.intro: The doctrine of sin prepares us for the gospel. This week we see sin's effects, false remedies and God's true remedy.

lessons.title: Bondage and blindness
lessons.body:
Sin is not just a mistake to correct; it is slavery. "Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin" (John 8:34). Unbelievers are "dead in trespasses and sins" (Ephesians 2:1), blinded by "the god of this world" (2 Corinthians 4:4).

Sin also spreads through families, communities and nations, producing injustice, corruption, violence and broken homes (Galatians 5:19-21).

This is why we cannot fix ourselves with resolutions, rituals or religion. Dead people need life; slaves need a redeemer.

lessons.title: False remedies
lessons.body:
People try many remedies for sin:

- **Good works:** "not by works of righteousness which we have done" (Titus 3:5).
- **Religious rituals:** sacrifices could never take away sins (Hebrews 10:4).
- **Comparison:** "they measuring themselves by themselves... are not wise" (2 Corinthians 10:12).
- **Denial:** "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves" (1 John 1:8).
- **Charms and sacrifices to spirits:** these add idolatry to sin.

None deals with guilt before God or changes the heart.

lessons.title: Where sin abounded, grace abounded
lessons.body:
God's remedy is Christ. "Where sin abounded, grace did much more abound" (Romans 5:20). Christ "bare our sins in his own body on the tree" (1 Peter 2:24) and gives new life through the Spirit.

As in Adam all die, "even so in Christ shall all be made alive" (1 Corinthians 15:22). The last Adam undoes what the first Adam did.

The right response to sin is repentance and faith: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness" (1 John 1:9). Later courses study salvation in detail.

terms.def: Slavery to sin, from which people cannot free themselves.
Separation from God's life because of sin.

short.q: Describe how the serpent tempted Eve.
short.model: He questioned God's word, denied God's warning of death, and slandered God's goodness by suggesting God was keeping something good from her.

short.q: Give three biblical words for sin and their meaning.
short.model: Missing the mark (falling short), transgression (crossing God's boundary), and iniquity (crookedness); also rebellion and trespass.

short.q: What is the difference between sins of commission and omission?
short.model: Commission is doing what God forbids; omission is failing to do what God commands.

short.q: Explain total depravity, including what it does not mean.
short.model: Sin affects every part of human nature so no one can save himself; it does not mean people are as evil as possible or never do outward good.

short.q: Summarise the two views of how Adam's sin affects us.
short.model: Federal headship: Adam represented us so his guilt is counted to all. Inherited corruption: we inherit a corrupt nature and become guilty when we personally sin.

short.q: Why can good works and rituals not remove sin?
short.model: They cannot remove guilt before a holy God or change a dead, enslaved heart; only Christ's work and God's grace can.

assignments.title: Genesis 3 and today
assignments.prompt: Show how the pattern of Genesis 3 (questioning God's word, desire, disobedience, shame, hiding and blame) appears in everyday temptation and sin today. Use at least three examples and close with God's remedy from the course.

assignments.title: Explaining sin to a friend
assignments.prompt: Write a short explanation of sin for a friend who says, "I'm a good person; I have never killed anyone." Use at least five Bible passages from this course, and end with the good news of Christ.
